newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash soymeal - Basis flat, demand still good.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash soymeal - Basis flat, demand still good.

text.p: Basis offers in cash soybean meal markets were steady Tuesday, underpinned by continued good demand in domestic and export markets, dealers said.
"People are still scrambling to meet contract needs, and as long as the exports hold up, we should stay firm in the near-term," an Indiana-based broker said.
The National Oilseed Processors Association reported Monday that last week's crushing pace was a healthy 30.6 million bushels.
That figure was above trade estimates, which ranged from 28.80 million to 30.00 million bushels.
The heavier-than-expected crush could pressure basis offers as exports begin to slow and supplies grow, some brokers said.
"It was a pretty decent crush," one Tennessee-based broker said. "I guess there's going to be a lot of meal out there."
One southeastern exporter was said to be selling soymeal in the domestic markets that was initially slated for export, cash sources said.
A Minnesota-based cash source reported that cash demand from producers remained solid, and demand for soymeal from Canada was also good.
"We've been extremely busy," the dealer said. "Cash business is very good."
